Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words. Open Air names the format and the freedom of it. The brand sits on the conditions under which sound carries best: clearly, with no walls in the way. Reads as a station, a network, and a stance.
Modern.industrySummary: Podcasting has become a serious media category. Top shows have brand-grade design systems and revenue to match. The bar for visual identity is high. New networks need to look like media companies on day one.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Pushkin (pushkin.fm) holds the founder-driven design-led network. Pineapple Street Studios (pineapple.fm) was the audio production benchmark. iHeartMedia (iheartmedia.com) is the volume player. We sit closest to Pushkin in design ambition.
Modern.positioningStatement: A podcast network for shows that are good enough to charge for.
Modern.positioningRationale: The market is full of mediocre podcasts. The opening is a network that only takes shows it would pay to subscribe to. The bar is the curatorial promise.

targetAudience.primary: Podcast hosts and producers building serious shows. Listeners who already pay for one subscription audio product. Advertisers who want premium-only inventory.

dos: Lead with the show, not the host
Skip the show-notes wall of text
donts: Run a trailer with stock music

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. OPEN AIR in a tight modern grotesk, all caps, two words on a single line with wide letter spacing. Square icon for app and social uses an OA monogram with a small dot above the O, like a broadcast signal.

colorPalette.name: Signal Orange
colorPalette.meaning: Broadcast accent. The dot on the studio sign.

typography.primary: Inter for the wordmark and product
typography.secondary: IBM Plex Mono for episode metadata
typography.rationale: Inter handles the marketing pages and product UI. The mono carries the run times, dates, and episode numbers. Two voices, one network.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No floating-head cover art. No celebrity guest pivots. No mid-roll stock-music ads. No clip-farm strategy.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: An app-first listening surface. Each show has its own micro-brand inside the network. Cover art follows a single grid. Episode descriptions are limited to 60 words.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Atticus is a name. It comes from antiquity and shows up again in literature. The word carries seriousness and a slight literary register. Naming a podcast network after a person, not a thing, makes it sound like the curator's voice is the brand.
Luxury.story: Atticus began with three founders who had spent a decade inside large media companies. They wanted to produce a small number of shows, very well, and listen to themselves more. The network has stayed at twelve shows since the beginning.
Luxury.industrySummary: Premium podcasts have been moving toward big-name guests and high production budgets. There's a smaller market for the literary side. Long form, narrative, considered, hosted by people who would have been magazine writers in another era.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Pushkin Industries (pushkin.fm) is the closest in literary register. Audible Originals (audible.com) holds the prestige-talent side. The New Yorker Radio Hour (newyorker.com/podcasts) does it under another brand. We sit in the same room as Pushkin, with fewer shows.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A podcast network for listeners who would have subscribed to a magazine.

targetAudience.primary: 35 to 65. Reads The Atlantic, The New Yorker, the London Review of Books. Pays for one or two cultural subscriptions. Listens on long walks, never on 2x speed.

dos: Address the listener as a reader
Run episodes long when they need to be
Send a quarterly printed program guide
donts: Cut episodes to fit ad breaks

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small period at the end of Atticus, like the end of a sentence, becomes the network's hallmark. The mark is used on covers, the printed program, and the brass plaque outside the studio.

typography.primary: Canela Text for the wordmark and editorial
typography.secondary: Söhne for the player and app UI
typography.rationale: A high contrast serif sets the literary tone. A modern grotesk handles the digital surfaces. Each does its job and stays quiet.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No celebrity-host shows added for traffic. No mid-roll programmatic ads. No clip strategy on social media. No promotional discount codes.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Tape is the oldest physical medium for recorded sound. Cassettes, reel-to-reel, the act of pressing record. The brand puts the original medium first, in a category that has gotten increasingly digital and decreasingly tangible.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most podcast networks compete on shows and personalities. There's an opening for one that competes on absence of clutter. No video. No clips. No vertical short-form. Just the audio.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most podcast platforms now bundle video. Substack (substack.com) has pulled some quiet listeners. The reference is closer to RadioPublic in spirit than to any big network.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A podcast network for the listener who only wants the audio.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who started listening to podcasts when there were only audio podcasts. They listen on a single app, in the background, while doing something else. They do not watch video clips.

dos: Use the smallest number of words
Show the run time and the date
Write episode descriptions in three sentences

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. TAPE in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps. No icon. The app icon is the wordmark in a tight square. No animations. No play-button graphics. Audio only, even in the brand.

typography.rationale: One face. The product is text, time, and play. Nothing decorative.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No video. No clips. No transcripts beyond what the show provides. No newsletter. No social media presence.

Corporate.tagline: Audio strategy for brands at scale.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Capital points to scale and seriousness. Audio names the category. Partners suggests the B2B service relationship. The whole name reads like a real, established audio production firm. The kind already on a Fortune 500 marketing-services panel.
Corporate.industrySummary: Branded audio is a serious B2B category. Companies want their own shows, sonic identities, internal audio comms, and audio-first ad campaigns. The category is mostly served by either large agencies (lacking specialism) or small podcast studios (lacking scale). The opening is a structured firm in the middle.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Pacific Content (pacific-content.com) is the branded-podcast peer. Industry Audio (industryaudio.com) sits in the same B2B production space. iHeart Studios (iheartmedia.com) covers the scale side. We are smaller and more strategic than iHeart, more structured than the boutiques.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A branded audio firm for enterprise clients that take audio seriously.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Most agencies treat audio as a tactic. Most podcast studios treat it as a service. We treat it as a strategic channel with measurable outcomes, formatted for procurement.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of Brand, CMOs, and Audio Marketing Leads at companies of 1000 to 50000 employees. They sign contracts for branded podcasts, sonic identities, internal-comms audio, and audio campaigns.
motivations: Audio that earns its budget line
One partner for strategy and production

dos: Show case studies with retention numbers
Speak to the buyer, not the listener

messagingPillars.name: Strategy first
messagingPillars.description: We start with the business problem, not the production calendar.

messagingPillars.name: Measurable outcomes
messagingPillars.description: Audio campaigns measured against retention, brand recall, and conversion. Reported quarterly.

messagingPillars.name: One partner across the audio stack
messagingPillars.description: Sonic identity, branded podcasts, internal audio communications, and audio media buying under one contract.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single sound wave reduced to three vertical bars at varying heights. Reads cleanly on procurement decks, name badges, and B2B trade shows.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed quarterly reports
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital and B2B portals. The serif handles formal quarterly business reviews.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No consumer podcasts. No celebrity-hosted shows. No public Spotify charts. No content marketing strategy. The firm sells through enterprise procurement, not social media.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. Says what the podcast is and is not. Not small talk. Not therapy. Big talk. The brand puts the conversation itself in the brand position. Loud, plain, and slightly cheeky.
Creative.manifesto: Most podcasts are scared of having an opinion. They hedge, they centrist, they cite three sources before saying anything. Big Talk is the network for shows whose hosts have something to say and aren't going to soften it for a sponsor.
Creative.industrySummary: Podcast brand has been cautious and clean. There's room for a network that's loud, opinionated, sticker-friendly, and still produces shows that hold up under criticism.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Barstool Sports (barstoolsports.com) has the loud-male side. The Ringer (theringer.com) holds the sports-culture middle. Crooked Media (crooked.com) does the political version. We sit somewhere between The Ringer and Pushkin in tone.
Creative.positioningStatement: A podcast network for shows that aren't afraid to be wrong on tape.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Has strong opinions about media, sports, technology, or culture. Listens to two or three shows weekly. Tells friends to listen. Wears the merch.

dos: Quote the worst lines from the hosts
Promote with real reactions from listeners
donts: Sand the edges off the hosts
Run sponsor reads that pretend to be content
Apologize for the shows we put out

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a bold display serif with a slight forward lean, like the words are leaning into the conversation. Standalone open-mouth icon for stickers, social profiles, and tap handles at the live recording bar.

colorPalette.name: Talk Red
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, stickers

colorPalette.name: Ink
colorPalette.usage: Body type, structure, wordmark on light

colorPalette.name: Hot Pink
colorPalette.meaning: Secondary accent. Used on alt-show covers.

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and metadata
typography.rationale: Migra has personality. Neue Montreal keeps the show titles readable. The pair feels designed and human.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a public radio network. Not afraid of red. Not too cool to put a quote on a tee.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Stickers on every laptop. Live recording nights at small bars in distribution cities. Hoodies that have the worst quote from the show on them. A weekly newsletter that's mostly listener emails.
